57% deployed. 11% delivering. The numbers tell the real AI story.

More than half of enterprises now have AI in production. But only 11% have achieved their top two goals. And workforce confidence is actually declining as adoption increases.

This is not a technology failure. The models work. The infrastructure is there. The gap is in execution — specifically in three areas most organizations underinvest in:

First, workflow integration. AI that is not embedded into how teams actually work stays on the shelf.

Second, outcome measurement. Without frameworks that connect AI outputs to business results, there is no feedback loop and no improvement.

Third, organizational readiness. If your people do not trust or understand the AI, adoption numbers are hollow.

Here is the opportunity: with most competitors spending on AI without capturing returns, the companies that solve execution first will pull ahead — not incrementally, but structurally.
